summary: Layer-granular placement of dense models larger than device memory: a planner over measured device, upload and host rates choosing between host execution of layers (AVX2/AVX-512 BF16 GEMVs, host KV) and double-buffered weight streaming, with measured selection of the plan
implementation_scope: C++ and CUDA host code: a planner predicting each placement's decode step from measured rates and ranking resident, host and streaming plans, with selection by timing the leading candidates; a two-slot weight streamer on a copy stream ordered by events; an executor running a step's layers by placement through an engine-supplied LayerRunner; measurements of pinned upload bandwidth, host GEMV rate and activation round trips; host BF16 GEMV with scalar, AVX2 and AVX-512 paths chosen at run time over a persistent thread pool, and a host pre-norm block with host KV; a synthetic model runner composing them with the batched reference engine's kernels and paged attention, plus a measurement tool; a Python model of the planner. A real model's layers and partial-layer offload are engine work.

agent_guidance.use_when: A dense model's weights do not fit the device memory left after KV cache and activations but fit host memory, and decode runs a single sequence or a few rows per step
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The model is expert routed, its weights fit the device, or quantizing them to fit stays within the quality budget
provides: A planner over measured rates (device bandwidth from crit eval probe, pinned upload, host GEMV, activation round trip) with predicted step times per placement
Measured selection among the leading candidate plans
A two-slot weight streamer: uploads of streamed layers two ahead on a copy stream, ordered by events
An executor for resident, streamed and host layers in one step, with one synchronization per run of host layers
Host BF16 GEMV on scalar, AVX2 or AVX-512 paths chosen through host-expert-arithmetic's host_isa.h over a thread pool, independent of the thread split
A host pre-norm block (RMSNorm, rotary, GQA attention over host KV, SiLU product) with the device's BF16 rounding points
Measurement helpers and a synthetic model runner with a measurement tool
engine_supplies: The model's layers as a LayerRunner (device and host forms of each layer over its own activations and KV)
Each layer's weights as one contiguous range in pinned host memory, and device copies of resident layers
The device budget for layer weights after KV cache, activations and other weights
preserve: A streamed layer is read only after its upload's event; its slot is reused only after release
Host layers read activations after the copy down completed; the device reads them after the copy back
A layer's KV cache lives where the layer runs
Plans ranked by prediction, chosen by measurement
adapt: Partial layers (only the MLP on the host), more staging slots, quantized host weights
Batched decode rows and prefill chunks on the host, NUMA-aware thread placement
Per-phase plans (prefill streaming, decode on the host)

code_files.purpose: Placements, measured rates, step prediction, candidate plans and measured selection
Weight streamer, layer runner interface, executor and measurement interfaces
Two-slot streaming, step execution by placement and rate measurements
Host GEMV ISAs, thread pool and the host pre-norm block
Scalar path, ISA dispatch, thread pool and host block operations
A complete LayerRunner: the synthetic transformer on device, streamed and host layers
Synthetic model weights, device and host layer forms, steps
Measures rates, predicts and times each candidate plan for a model above the budget
Python model of the prediction and candidate plans

requires.hardware: CUDA C++20; x86-64 with AVX2 or AVX-512F for the fast host paths (a scalar path runs elsewhere); pinned host memory for the weights; Python 3.11+ standard library for the planner model
requires.model: Dense decoder layers whose weights form one contiguous range each
requires.workload: Decode with one sequence or a few rows per step, weights above the device budget

contract.input: Layer byte sizes, the device budget and measured rates for planning; pinned host weights, device copies of resident layers and a LayerRunner for execution
contract.output: Ranked plans with predicted step times; each step's layers executed by placement
contract.ownership: The engine owns weights, activations, KV caches and streams; the weight streamer owns its two slots and events; the thread pool owns its workers
contract.failure: Planning without layers or with non-positive rates, a streamed layer larger than a slot, a store that disagrees with the plan, or host GEMV geometry the ISA cannot run throws invalid_argument; CUDA errors throw runtime_error
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; device rates come from crit eval probe

dependencies: host-expert-arithmetic's host_isa (crit_host_isa) for run-time ISA detection
batched-reference-engine for the synthetic model runner
Python standard library for the planner model

validation.host: The README example and test_reusable_techniques.py: candidate order and predicted times of the planner model
validation.native: Planner candidates and predictions, measured selection overriding the predicted order; scalar, AVX2 and AVX-512 host GEMVs within 1e-5 of FP64 and bit for bit across thread splits; a six-layer synthetic model under resident, streamed (slots recycled), host and mixed placements: streamed logits equal resident ones bit for bit, host placements within 2% (at most 1.3% all on host, sm_120)
validation.performance: One machine (RTX 5090, 12 host threads with AVX-512), 16 layers of 436 MB, device budget set below the weights: rates device 1,131 GB/s, upload 28.8 GB/s, host GEMV 35 GB/s, round trip 21 us; 25% resident: host 12 layers predicted 147 ms / measured 171 ms per decode step, streaming 14 layers 214 / 212 ms; 60% resident: 91 / 94 ms and 139 / 137 ms; host execution selected; no claim for other machines
